title: Lifestyle and Dietary Factors Associated with Obesity Levels
text:
Obesity is a major public health concern associated with multiple demographic, dietary, and lifestyle factors. Understanding the factors associated with different obesity levels may contribute to a better understanding of behavioral and health-related patterns.



To what extent are demographic characteristics, dietary habits, and lifestyle factors associated with ordered obesity levels among individuals from Mexico, Peru, and Colombia?



The objectives of this study are to:

Describe the distribution of obesity levels in the dataset.
Examine demographic, dietary, and lifestyle characteristics.
Evaluate associations between these characteristics and ordered obesity levels.
Compare ordinal logistic regression models.
Assess model assumptions and diagnostic results.

2.2 Outcome Variable
The outcome variable is NObeyesdad, an ordered categorical variable with seven levels, ranging from insufficient weight to obesity type III.

title: Lifestyle and Dietary Factors Associated with Obesity Levels
text:
2.3 Statistical Analysis
Ordinal logistic regression will be used to examine the associations between demographic, dietary, and lifestyle factors and obesity levels.
Model comparison, parameter estimation, and diagnostic assessment will be conducted.

title: Lifestyle and Dietary Factors Associated with Obesity Levels
text:
2.4 Data Preparation
The dataset was obtained from the UCI Machine Learning Repository and imported into R using the readr package.
The dataset contains 2,111 observations and 17 variables. No missing values were identified during the initial data inspection.
The outcome variable, NObeyesdad, was converted into an ordered factor with seven levels, ranging from Insufficient Weight to Obesity Type III.
The variables Height and Weight were excluded from the primary regression models because body-size information is directly related to the construction of obesity categories. Including these variables could introduce target leakage.

title: Lifestyle and Dietary Factors Associated with Obesity Levels
text:
2.5 Analytical Dataset


Code
# Load required packages
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

# Import the dataset
obesity_data <- read_csv(
  "data/ObesityDataSet_raw_and_data_sinthetic.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Define the ordered outcome variable
obesity_data$NObeyesdad <- factor(
  obesity_data$NObeyesdad,
  levels = c(
    "Insufficient_Weight",
    "Normal_Weight",
    "Overweight_Level_I",
    "Overweight_Level_II",
    "Obesity_Type_I",
    "Obesity_Type_II",
    "Obesity_Type_III"
  ),
  ordered = TRUE
)

# Check dataset dimensions
dim(obesity_data)


[1] 2111   17


Code
# Check missing values
sum(is.na(obesity_data))


[1] 0

The dataset included 2,111 observations distributed across seven ordered obesity categories. Obesity Type I was the most frequent category (n = 351, 16.6%), whereas Insufficient Weight was the least frequent category (n = 272, 12.9%).
The distribution was relatively balanced across the seven outcome categories, with percentages ranging from 12.9% to 16.6%.

2.6.1 Define Dietary and Lifestyle Variables


Code
# Define categorical dietary and lifestyle variables
categorical_vars <- c(
  "FAVC",
  "CAEC",
  "SMOKE",
  "SCC",
  "CALC",
  "MTRANS"
)

# Define numerical or ordinal-coded variables
numeric_vars <- c(
  "FCVC",
  "NCP",
  "CH2O",
  "FAF",
  "TUE"
)

# Convert categorical predictors to factors

obesity_data <- obesity_data |>
  mutate(
    Gender = factor(Gender),
    family_history_with_overweight =
      factor(family_history_with_overweight),
    FAVC = factor(FAVC),
    CAEC = factor(CAEC),
    SMOKE = factor(SMOKE),
    SCC = factor(SCC),
    CALC = factor(CALC),
    MTRANS = factor(MTRANS)
  )
